atoms.text: This guide configures the FrameForge transcoding service to read source video masters from the bucket acme-media-masters and write encoded renditions back to the same bucket. The service runs under the IAM role FrameForgeTranscodeRole in account 111122223333. Access is granted only through an identity-based policy attached to that role, and the bucket policy is not changed. Create a policy with one statement that allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-media-masters/masters/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-media-masters/renditions/*. Add a second statement that allows s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::acme-media-masters with an s3:prefix condition of masters/*. Attach the policy to FrameForgeTranscodeRole. The existing bucket policy contains no statement that names the role, and because the role and the bucket are in the same account, the role's own policy is sufficient. To verify, submit a job for masters/promo-001.mov and confirm that renditions/promo-001/1080p.mp4 appears in the bucket. If the job fails with AccessDenied, check that the policy is attached and that no permissions boundary or explicit deny applies.

This guide configures the FrameForge transcoding service to read source video masters from the bucket acme-media-masters and write encoded renditions back to the same bucket. The service runs under the IAM role FrameForgeTranscodeRole in account 111122223333. Access is granted only by statements in the bucket's resource-based policy, and the role's identity-based policies are not changed. Add a bucket policy statement whose Principal is the role ARN arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/FrameForgeTranscodeRole, allowing s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-media-masters/masters/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-media-masters/renditions/*. Add a second statement for the same principal that allows s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::acme-media-masters with an s3:prefix condition of masters/*. Save the bucket policy. The role has no S3 statements for this bucket in its attached policies, and because the role and the bucket are in the same account, the bucket policy is sufficient. To verify, submit a job for masters/promo-001.mov and confirm that renditions/promo-001/1080p.mp4 appears in the bucket. If the job fails with AccessDenied, check that the Principal ARN matches the role exactly and that no explicit deny applies.

This guide lets the ScanLift OCR batch worker read scanned PDF files from the bucket acme-scans-inbox and write extracted text files to the same bucket. The worker authenticates as the IAM user ocr-batch-user using long-term access keys stored on the processing host. Access is granted only through an identity-based policy attached to that user, and the bucket policy is not changed. Write a policy that allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-scans-inbox/incoming/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-scans-inbox/text/*. Include a statement allowing s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::acme-scans-inbox restricted to the incoming/ prefix. Attach the policy directly to ocr-batch-user or to a group the user belongs to. Do not add any statement for this user to the bucket policy. Run the worker against incoming/invoice-4471.pdf and confirm that text/invoice-4471.txt is created. A 403 response usually means the policy is not attached or the object key is outside the allowed prefixes.

This guide lets the ScanLift OCR batch worker read scanned PDF files from the bucket acme-scans-inbox and write extracted text files to the same bucket. The worker authenticates as the IAM user ocr-batch-user using long-term access keys stored on the processing host. Access is granted only by statements in the bucket's resource-based policy, and the user's identity-based policies are not changed. Add a bucket policy statement whose Principal is the user ARN arn:aws:iam::111122223333:user/ocr-batch-user, allowing s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-scans-inbox/incoming/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-scans-inbox/text/*. Include a second statement for the same principal allowing s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::acme-scans-inbox restricted to the incoming/ prefix. Do not attach any S3 policy to the user or to its groups. Run the worker against incoming/invoice-4471.pdf and confirm that text/invoice-4471.txt is created. A 403 response usually means the Principal ARN is misspelled or the object key is outside the allowed prefixes.

This guide grants an image thumbnail generator access to a bucket used for user-uploaded photographs. The generator runs as the IAM role ThumbGenRole and reads originals from the bucket acme-photo-store under uploads/ and writes resized JPEG and WebP derivatives under thumbs/. Access is granted only through an identity-based policy on the role, and the bucket policy is left unchanged. Create a managed policy allowing s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-photo-store/uploads/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-photo-store/thumbs/*. Add s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN with a prefix condition for uploads/. Attach the managed policy to ThumbGenRole and confirm the role's trust policy allows the compute environment to assume it. The bucket policy remains as it was and contains no statement for this role. Upload uploads/sample.png and check that thumbs/sample-256.webp is written within a few seconds. If no output appears, review the role's attached policies and any permissions boundary.

This guide grants an image thumbnail generator access to a bucket used for user-uploaded photographs. The generator runs as the IAM role ThumbGenRole and reads originals from the bucket acme-photo-store under uploads/ and writes resized JPEG and WebP derivatives under thumbs/. Access is granted only by the bucket's resource-based policy, and the role's identity-based policies are left unchanged. Add a bucket policy statement whose Principal is arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/ThumbGenRole, allowing s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-photo-store/uploads/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-photo-store/thumbs/*. Add s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN for the same principal with a prefix condition for uploads/. Confirm the role's trust policy allows the compute environment to assume it, but attach no S3 permissions to the role. The role's attached policies remain as they were and contain no S3 statements for this bucket. Upload uploads/sample.png and check that thumbs/sample-256.webp is written within a few seconds. If no output appears, review the bucket policy's Principal value and any explicit deny.

This guide gives an audio loudness normalization job access to raw recordings and a destination for processed files. The job runs as the IAM role LoudNormRole and reads WAV files from acme-audio-pipeline under raw/ and writes normalized FLAC files under normalized/. Access is granted only through an identity-based policy attached to the role, and the bucket policy is not modified. Define a policy that allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-audio-pipeline/raw/* and s3:PutObject plus s3:AbortMultipartUpload on arn:aws:s3:::acme-audio-pipeline/normalized/*. Add s3:ListBucket on the bucket with a condition limiting s3:prefix to raw/. Attach the policy to LoudNormRole. The bucket policy has no statement naming this role, and the same-account role policy alone determines access. Because FLAC outputs can exceed 100 MB, the job uses multipart uploads, so confirm the abort permission is present. Process raw/session-12.wav and verify that normalized/session-12.flac is complete.

Define a bucket policy statement whose Principal is arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/LoudNormRole, allowing s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-audio-pipeline/raw/* and s3:PutObject plus s3:AbortMultipartUpload on arn:aws:s3:::acme-audio-pipeline/normalized/*. Add a statement for the same principal allowing s3:ListBucket on the bucket with a condition limiting s3:prefix to raw/. The role has no S3 permissions of its own, and the same-account bucket policy alone determines access. This guide configures a subtitle burn-in worker that reads video files and matching SRT caption files and writes captioned video back to storage. The worker signs requests as the IAM user captionwriter in account 111122223333. It reads from the bucket acme-video-captions under source/ and writes results under burned/. Access is granted only through an identity-based policy attached to the user, and the bucket policy is not changed. Create a policy allowing s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-video-captions/source/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-video-captions/burned/*, and add s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN limited to the source/ prefix. Attach the policy to captionwriter. Keep the bucket policy as it is, with no statement for this user. Test with source/lecture-09.mp4 and source/lecture-09.srt, and confirm that burned/lecture-09.mp4 is produced. If the worker reports AccessDenied for the .srt file, check that the policy resource covers the full source/ prefix.

This guide configures a subtitle burn-in worker that reads video files and matching SRT caption files and writes captioned video back to storage. The worker signs requests as the IAM user captionwriter in account 111122223333. It reads from the bucket acme-video-captions under source/ and writes results under burned/. Access is granted only by the bucket's resource-based policy, and the user's identity-based policies are not changed. Add a bucket policy statement whose Principal is arn:aws:iam::111122223333:user/captionwriter, allowing s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-video-captions/source/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-video-captions/burned/*, and add s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN limited to the source/ prefix. Do not attach any S3 policy to captionwriter. Test with source/lecture-09.mp4 and source/lecture-09.srt, and confirm that burned/lecture-09.mp4 is produced. If the worker reports AccessDenied for the .srt file, check that the policy resource covers the full source/ prefix.

This guide sets up a document watermarking service that reads draft contracts and writes watermarked copies for external review. The service runs as the IAM role MarkStampRole and uses the bucket acme-legal-docs. It reads from drafts/ and writes PDF output to watermarked/. Access is granted only through an identity-based policy attached to the role, and the bucket policy is not changed. In the policy, allow s3:GetObject and s3:GetObjectVersion on arn:aws:s3:::acme-legal-docs/drafts/*, and allow s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-legal-docs/watermarked/*. Add s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN with a prefix condition of drafts/. Attach the policy to MarkStampRole and verify that the role's session duration covers the longest batch run. The bucket policy remains unchanged and contains no statement for MarkStampRole. Submit drafts/nda-2024.pdf and confirm that watermarked/nda-2024.pdf is written with the expected version metadata. A failure on versioned reads usually indicates a missing s3:GetObjectVersion action.

The service runs as the IAM role MarkStampRole and uses the bucket acme-legal-docs. It reads from drafts/ and writes PDF output to watermarked/. Access is granted only by the bucket's resource-based policy, and the role's identity-based policies are not changed. In the bucket policy, add a statement with the Principal arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/MarkStampRole that allows s3:GetObject and s3:GetObjectVersion on arn:aws:s3:::acme-legal-docs/drafts/*, and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-legal-docs/watermarked/*. Add s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN for the same principal with a prefix condition of drafts/. Save the policy and verify that the role's session duration covers the longest batch run. The role keeps no S3 permissions in its attached policies. Submit drafts/nda-2024.pdf and confirm that watermarked/nda-2024.pdf is written with the expected version metadata. A failure on versioned reads usually indicates a missing s3:GetObjectVersion action.

This guide enables an e-book conversion tool to turn manuscript files into EPUB packages using one bucket. The tool authenticates as the IAM user epub-converter and reads DOCX manuscripts from the bucket acme-publishing under manuscripts/. It writes the EPUB output and a JSON validation report under epub/. Access is granted only through an identity-based policy on the user, and the bucket policy is not changed. Create a policy that allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-publishing/manuscripts/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-publishing/epub/*. Add s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::acme-publishing restricted to the manuscripts/ prefix. Attach the policy to epub-converter and rotate the access key if it is older than 90 days. The bucket policy has no statement for this user. Convert manuscripts/novel-draft.docx and confirm that epub/novel-draft.epub and epub/novel-draft-report.json both exist. If the report is missing, check that the PutObject resource covers the entire epub/ prefix.

Add s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::acme-publishing for the same principal, restricted to the manuscripts/ prefix. Rotate the access key if it is older than 90 days. The user has no S3 policy attached directly or through groups. Convert manuscripts/novel-draft.docx and confirm that epub/novel-draft.epub and epub/novel-draft-report.json both exist. If the report is missing, check that the PutObject resource in the bucket policy covers the entire epub/ prefix.

This guide grants a live-stream packaging service access to recorded segments and a location for adaptive streaming output. The service runs as the IAM role SegmentPackRole and reads MPEG-TS segments from the bucket acme-live-archive under segments/. It writes HLS playlists and fragmented MP4 files under packaged/. Access is granted only through an identity-based policy attached to the role, and the bucket policy is not changed. Add a policy allowing s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-live-archive/segments/* and s3:PutObject and s3:DeleteObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-live-archive/packaged/*, since playlists are rewritten as the stream advances. Include s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN restricted to the segments/ prefix. Attach the policy to SegmentPackRole. The bucket policy remains as it was and has no statement naming the role. Start a test event and verify that packaged/event-33/index.m3u8 updates every few seconds. If playlist updates stop, confirm the delete permission is present and no permissions boundary blocks it.
